title: Military Police Investigator (MPI) (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS (5811), DC I&L
raw_text:
7. MOS 5819, Military Police Investigator (MPI) (GySgt to Cpl) NMOS (5811),
DC I&L

    a. Summary. The duties of the MPI require the assignment of mature and
intelligent individuals responsible for investigating criminal violations of
the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ) in matters of interest to the
United States Marine Corps.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must currently hold MOS 5811.

        (2) Must have a minimum of one year military police experience to be
considered for the Military Police Investigator Course.

        (3) Accreditation of MPI will be accomplished by the provost marshal/
police chief on an as needed basis, through the issuance of law enforcement
branch produced investigator serialized credentials approved by CMC, DC I&L.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Military Police Investigator Course (A1658J3), U.S.
Army Military Police School, Ft Leonard Wood, MO.

        (2) Accreditation of MPI will be accomplished by the provost Marshal
on an as needed basis, through the issuance of locally produced serialized
credentials approved by CMC (PS).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ac), Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections Training and
Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Detectives and Criminal Investigators 33-3021.

            (2) Police and Sheriff's Patrol Officers 33-3051.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Criminal Investigator, 5821.

The Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections OccFld provides the installation commander continuous support by enforcing the law, preventing and suppressing crime, assessing command physical security posture, preserving military control, quelling disturbances, investigating offenses, apprehending offenders, protecting property and personnel, investigating traffic accidents, controlling traffic, providing first response to active shooters incidents and special response to a barricaded subject, guarding military prisoners and supervising brig operations and correctional custody units. Provide the MARFORRES Commander support to security and mobility operations, battlefield circulation and traffic control, rear area security operations to include limited offensive and defensive combat operations, detention operations to include handling and safeguarding prisoners of war, refugees, or evacuees, guarding military prisoners, and returning absentees/deserters to military control.
